Review accepted 3B across text sizes

This is the accepted unfolded screen only: soft neutral current-track container, bold current title, tonal Open, and transport 1B. The mode selector now uses the fewest connected rows whose complete labels fit.

Native Android · 50% to 200%

What changed and what stayed fixed

  1. Direct device setting: the target emulator stored font_scale=0.5, so the requested 50% capture is used rather than a substitute.
  2. Dynamic mode label: the third option always names the active subdirectory. Every capture says Shuffle Camellia.
  3. Adaptive row count: complete labels try one connected row, then a connected 2×2 block, then four connected vertical rows. No state scrolls horizontally.
  4. Accepted 3B: every capture retains the T3 current row, O2 tonal Open, centered transport, 24% seek position, outlined Previous and Next, and filled Pause.
  5. Native evidence: every image is an opaque 2076 × 2152px Compose capture of the 852 × 883dp unfolded Pixel 9 Pro Fold with Android system bars and live insets.

Observed wrapping

50% and 75% use one row. 100% and 150% use 2×2. 200% uses four rows.

Padding behavior

The control tries Material's 12dp horizontal content padding first, then 6dp before adding rows. Targets remain at least 48dp.

Assistive technology boundary

Native semantics expose four radio options and the current-track description. Production assistive technology must still verify one mutually exclusive group announcement.

Priority: one row > two rows > four rows. One row preserves the most deck space; two rows ranks next because it preserves more space than four; four rows is the fallback that keeps every label complete. This is one adaptive design, not five competing visual options.

Exact accepted screen at each requested scale

Open any capture to inspect it at Fit, 1dp per CSS pixel, or native panel pixels.

50% · one row

Minimum requested scale

Default Material content padding fits all four labels in one connected row.

Pros
  • One mode row preserves maximum deck space.
  • More folder and track content is visible.
Cons
  • Text is intentionally smaller than the normal setting.
75% · one row

Compact one-row padding

Full available width plus 6dp horizontal content padding keeps Shuffle Camellia complete.

Pros
  • All labels remain complete in one row.
  • Targets remain at least 48dp.
Cons
  • Inner horizontal padding falls from the Material default 12dp to 6dp.
100% · connected 2×2

Default Android scale

One row clips the named Shuffle option even after compact padding, so the control uses two rows.

Pros
  • The complete current-subdirectory label remains visible.
  • The 2×2 block uses half the rows of the vertical fallback.
Cons
  • The mode control now occupies two rows at the default scale.
150% · connected 2×2

Enlarged text

Compact content padding keeps two segments per row without clipping.

Pros
  • 2×2 preserves deck height while retaining complete labels.
  • All four mode targets remain connected.
Cons
  • Less folder and track content fits in each pane.
200% · four rows

Largest requested scale

Shuffle Camellia cannot share a half-width row without clipping, so every segment gets one row.

Pros
  • Every mode label remains complete at the largest scale.
  • The full control clears the navigation inset.
Cons
  • Four rows use the most deck height.
  • The deck must scroll vertically to expose its complete lower state.
